mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous 12-month average - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its previous 12-month high by at least 3% for three consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero in more than 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) drop below 3.5% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth exceeds its 12-month moving average by more than 1 standard deviation signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage inflation and ultimately pressures equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the effect reverses when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three months signals a deflationary risk, which discourages investment and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 12-mo MA - 1.5% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or inflation expectations rise above 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1.5% alongside a concurrent rise in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% signals strengthening consumer and housing demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 1.5% AND HOUST > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically positive in more than 60% of triggered months, or the effect reverses during a concurrent spike in interest rates.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for four consecutive months, with no corresponding rise in wage growth (implied by stable CPIAUCSL), signals a labor market mismatch that may precede wage inflation and higher costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 4 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL change ≈ 0%
regime_hint: tight labor market with stable prices
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation accelerates above 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.8% for two consecutive months signals a broad-based supply shock, which raises input costs and reduces corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong demand growth.
